main.description: A cultural place as a publishing party: a venue, gallery, rehearsal room, recording studio, artist studio, makerspace, supplier or shop — anywhere the public can visit or book. Supersedes com.cultureblocs.venue.profile, which covered only venues; a venue is now a place whose spaceTypes include 'venue'. This record is for spaces open to the public or bookable by them. A person working from home publishes a creative.profile (an area, never an address) and offers through com.cultureblocs.offer; they do not publish a place. Nothing about a visitor is ever collected here.

spaceTypes.description: What kind of place this is. A list, because real places mix uses: a railway-arch building can be a gallery, artist studios and a shop at once. Advisory vocabulary: readers show unknown values as tags rather than dropping them.

publicAccess.description: How the public reaches this place. 'online_only' places (a supplier with no shop) publish serviceArea and no location.

location.description: Where the place is, using the shared location objects of the open social web. Places are public, so precision is normally exact. Omit for online_only places.

area.description: The named area the place sits in (town, borough), normally derived from the postcode by the publishing app. Lets readers filter by area without geocoding.

serviceArea.description: Areas the place serves beyond its own doors: delivery, mobile services, 'UK-wide'. The main location field for online_only places.

capacity.description: Approximate standing/seated capacity, where it applies. Small venues are repeatedly asked for this by funders and licensing.

accessibility.description: Freeform access notes: step-free entry, accessible toilet, hearing loop, quiet room.

hours.description: Freeform opening or booking hours, e.g. 'Tue–Sat 10–6', '24-hour self-service'.

images.description: Photos of the place. The first is used on directory cards.

externalIds.description: Wikidata, MusicBrainz place, charity or company number.

createdAt.description: When this record was first stamped. The only immutable field: everything else may be revised by publishing a new commit.
